answer: Yes! LV(Logical) has to be less than or equal to size of VG.(Virtual)  which must be <= Physical
description:
Introduction

LVM stands for Logical Volume Management. It is a system of managing logical volumes, or filesystems, that is much more advanced and flexible than the traditional method of partitioning a disk into one or more segments and formatting that partition with a filesystem.

There are 3 concepts that LVM manages:
Physical Volumes
Volume Groups
Logical Volumes

LVM Visual Representation

Assume we have two Physical Volume with size 5.5GB and 3.7GB.
Now we combine them to form a Volume Group of size 5.5 + 3.7 = 9.2GB Now we can create Logical volumes of different sizes on the top of this Volume Group.
Here's Viusal representation of how LVM works Based on Size, can we say LV <= VG <= PV ?
name: Setting up LVM in Linux

description:
Now you some basic concept.Ready ? Let's go...
Here is my hard disk details.

fdisk -l 
                                              

Disk /dev/ubdb: 6442 MB, 6442450944 bytes
255 heads, 63 sectors/track, 783 cylinders
Units = cylinders of 16065 * 512 = 8225280 bytes
Sector size (logical/physical): 512 bytes / 512 bytes
I/O size (minimum/optimal): 512 bytes / 512 bytes
Disk identifier: 0x00000000


Disk /dev/ubdc: 4294 MB, 4294967296 bytes
255 heads, 63 sectors/track, 522 cylinders
Units = cylinders of 16065 * 512 = 8225280 bytes
Sector size (logical/physical): 512 bytes / 512 bytes
I/O size (minimum/optimal): 512 bytes / 512 bytes
Disk identifier: 0x00000000


Disk /dev/ubde: 8589 MB, 8589934592 bytes
255 heads, 63 sectors/track, 1044 cylinders
Units = cylinders of 16065 * 512 = 8225280 bytes
Sector size (logical/physical): 512 bytes / 512 bytes
I/O size (minimum/optimal): 512 bytes / 512 bytes
Disk identifier: 0x00000000
We are going to create LVM using two partitions, /dev/ubdb which has 6GB(or 6442 MB) and /dev/ubdc which has 4GB(or 4294 MB) space.
In order to Create LVM , you need to three steps Physical volume,Volume group and Logical Volume.
Physical volume can be set of hard disk partitions and these partition combined together to form a Volume group. Logical volume is final resulting partition built from Volume group.
First ensure, we have lvm tools by installing this package
yum -y install system-config-lvm
name: Choosing drives for LVM

description:
Step 1: Creating Physical Volumes.


The command pvcreate is used to initialize the partitions (/dev/ubdb and /dev/ubdc) for use by LVM. So execute it on our partition like this,
pvcreate /dev/ubdb /dev/ubdc 
  Physical volume "/dev/sdb" successfully created
  Physical volume "/dev/sdc" successfully created
Though above output shows Physical volume successfully created on our dis, We can recheck them using the command called pvscan which scans for list of physical volumes that can support LVM setup. pvscan 

  PV /dev/sdb         lvm2 [6.00 GiB]
  PV /dev/sdc         lvm2 [4.00 GiB]
  Total: 2 [10.00 GiB] / in use: 0 [0   ] / in no VG: 2 [10.00 GiB]
Yeah,we are sure that two partitions are ready.
name: Create PV

description:
Step 2: Now,Create Volume Group over Physical volumes


The command to create new volume group is vgcreate - yes,you are right,it\'s very much similar to previous command pvcreate thus makes it easy to remember them. Following vgcreate command creates a new volume group called giis_vol_grp using the block special device (/dev/ubdb and /dev/ubdc) previously configured for LVM with pvcreate.
vgcreate giis_vol_grp /dev/ubdb /dev/ubdc 
 

  Volume group "giis_vol_grp" successfully created

We can display attributes of volume groups as shown below.Note the total size of giis_vol_grp volume group is sum of /dev/ubdb and /dev/ubdc ,that's 6GB + 4Gb = 10GB.(approx) 
[root@localhost ~]# vgdisplay 
  --- Volume group ---
  VG Name               giis_vol_grp
  System ID             
  Format                lvm2
  Metadata Areas        2
  Metadata Sequence No  1
  VG Access             read/write
  VG Status             resizable
  MAX LV                0
  Cur LV                0
  Open LV               0
  Max PV                0
  Cur PV                2
  Act PV                2
  VG Size               9.99 GiB
  PE Size               4.00 MiB
  Total PE              2558
  Alloc PE / Size       0 / 0   
  Free  PE / Size       2558 / 9.99 GiB
  VG UUID               cgsRO4-2dBC-3wSt-zXUl-8XCW-j5Ff-ldCpY1
name: Create VG

description:
Step 3: Finally,Create Logical Volume On Volume Group.


By now you should know what lvcreate will do? right? here it's ,lvcreate creates a new logical volume from a volume group. Here we can specify the size of logical volume based on our requirement.We have used physical extents (see above PE size is 4MB) to specify the size 50*4MB=200MB.You can also use --size option with lvcreate to specify the actual size. lvcreate -l 5 -n vol1 giis_vol_grp 
  Logical volume "vol1" created
Now from the attributes of a logical volume,we can see it's size is set as 200MB. lvdisplay 
  --- Logical volume ---
  LV Path                /dev/giis_vol_grp/vol1
  LV Name                vol1
  VG Name                giis_vol_grp
  LV UUID                PiQZby-SAMN-4S1n-wCgK-huXy-DcLq-OCkqhd
  LV Write Access        read/write
  LV Creation host, time ip-172-31-13-180, 2014-12-25 09:43:15 +0000
  LV Status              available
  # open                 0
  LV Size                200.00 MiB
  Current LE             50
  Segments               1
  Allocation             inherit
  Read ahead sectors     auto
  - currently set to     256
  Block device           253:0
That's it.Now we can create a file system on the logical volume.We create ext3fs for this example.
name: Create LV

description:
Step 4:Creating File system on Logical Volume


[root@localhost ~]# mkfs.ext3 /dev/giis_vol_grp/vol1
now mount it under /mnt/vol1 (mkdir -p /mnt/vol1)
[root@localhost ~]# mount /dev/giis_vol_grp/vol1 /mnt/vol1
Just check it's size. 
# df -h /mnt
Filesystem                     Size  Used Avail Use% Mounted on
/dev/mapper/giis_vol_grp-vol1  194M  5.6M  179M   4% /mnt/1
name: Creating FS on LV

description:
Say for example,Now I have created two logical volumes named "vol2" with 20MB and "vol3" with 30MB and formatted it as ext3fs and mounted them with following commands.

lvcreate --name vol2 --size 20M giis_vol_grp
lvcreate --name vol3 --size 30M giis_vol_grp

Type lvdisplay to view new logical volume information. Format new volumes vol2 and vol3

mkfs.ext3 /dev/giis_vol_grp/vol2
mkfs.ext3 /dev/giis_vol_grp/vol3

and mount them like.

mount /dev/giis_vol_grp/vol2 /mnt/vol2
mount /dev/giis_vol_grp/vol3 /mnt/vol3
name: Add two more LV

description:
Two months later,we found, vol3 doesn't need 3GB and 1GB is enough. And vol1 needs extra 1GB.Following represents the currents status of LVM 
[root@localhost ~]# lvscan
  ACTIVE            '/dev/giis_vol_grp/vol1' [200.00 MiB] inherit
  ACTIVE            '/dev/giis_vol_grp/vol2' [2.00 GiB] inherit
  ACTIVE            '/dev/giis_vol_grp/vol3' [3.00 GiB] inherit

Shrinking size
So first we reduce/shrink "vol3" from 3GB to 1GB using lvreduce command.

lvreduce -L 10M /dev/giis_vol_grp/vol3 
  WARNING: Reducing active logical volume to 1.00 GiB
  THIS MAY DESTROY YOUR DATA (filesystem etc.)
Do you really want to reduce vol3? [y/n]: y
  Size of logical volume giis_vol_grp/vol3 changed from 3.00 GiB (768 extents) to 1.00 GiB (256 extents).
  Logical volume vol3 successfully resized
As you can see from above ,the "vol3" is shrinked to 10MB. Use lvscan to verify it. lvscan 

  ACTIVE            '/dev/giis_vol_grp/vol1' [200.00 MiB] inherit
  ACTIVE            '/dev/giis_vol_grp/vol2' [2.00 GiB] inherit
  ACTIVE            '/dev/giis_vol_grp/vol3' [1.00 GiB] inherit
name: Two months Later..Shrink

description:
After three months, we found found vol1 has not enough space. We need to add more space to it.
Increasing size
Now we increase the "vol1" to 2GB using lvresize command.
lvresize -L 40M /dev/giis_vol_grp/vol1 
  Size of logical volume giis_vol_grp/vol1 changed from 200.00 MiB (50 extents) to 2.00 GiB (512 extents).
  Logical volume vol1 successfully resized
Finally we got the required size,where "vol1" is increased from 20MB to 40MB and "vol3" size reduced from 3GB to 1GB.
lvscan 
  ACTIVE            '/dev/giis_vol_grp/vol1' [2.00 GiB] inherit
  ACTIVE            '/dev/giis_vol_grp/vol2' [2.00 GiB] inherit
  ACTIVE            '/dev/giis_vol_grp/vol3' [1.00 GiB] inherit
name: Three months Later...Extend

description:
Snapshot

Lets protect vol3 by creating clone/snapshot of its data.
lvcreate --size 8M --snapshot --name snap_vol3 /dev/giis_vol_grp/vol3 
  Logical volume "snap_vol3" created
Snapshot status of this logical volume vol3 can be viewed with
lvdisplay /dev/giis_vol_grp/vol3

description:
finally quick report of our logical and volume groups using lvs and pvs command.
lvs 

  LV        VG           Attr       LSize Pool Origin Data%  Meta%  Move Log Cpy%Sync Convert
  snap_vol3 giis_vol_grp swi-a-s--- 1.00g      vol3   0.00                                   
  vol1      giis_vol_grp -wi-ao---- 2.00g                                                    
  vol2      giis_vol_grp -wi-a----- 2.00g                                                    
  vol3      giis_vol_grp owi-a-s--- 1.00g

and to view Physical Group status
pvs 

  PV         VG           Fmt  Attr PSize PFree   
  /dev/sdb   giis_vol_grp lvm2 a--  6.00g 1020.00m
  /dev/sdc   giis_vol_grp lvm2 a--  4.00g    3.00g
